samples.summary: Toolbar style dropdown still labels a bulleted heading "Normal text" (and targets the `normal` named style)
samples.evidence: `getBlockLabel(blockType.type, blockType.headingLevel)` (text-style-group.tsx:86) and `blockTypeToStyleId(...)` (line 89) both gate on `type === "heading"` (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-style-options.ts:112,127). With the new invariant a bulleted Heading 2 is `{type:'list-item', headingLevel:2}`, so the dropdown shows "Normal text" and `currentStyleId` resolves to `normal` — while the model (and Enter/Backspace/toggle exits, per the diff) treats the block as a Heading 2. The "Update <style> to match" action in the same menu therefore redefines Normal text from a block the editor considers a heading. The fix likely belongs in the frontend label/style-id helpers (or in a deliberate decision to keep the level invisible, which the `Block` doc comment asserts but the diff's Google-Docs-parity rationale contradicts).

samples.summary: `blockStyleId` maps every list-item to `normal`, so a "bulleted heading" renders as body text and only jumps back to heading metrics when the list is removed
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:99-113 returns `'normal'` for `list-item` regardless of `headingLevel`; layout/inline resolution (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts, resolveStyleInline) and spacing materialization (named-styles.ts:150) both key off it. The diff's stated parity goal is that the bullet is applied *to* the heading, but on this branch bulleting a Heading 2 visibly demotes it to body size/spacing, and un-bulleting re-materializes heading spacing (memory.ts:272-274), overwriting any custom spacing the user set while it was a bullet. Behaviour change to a shared exported symbol's consumers that the diff does not address.

samples.summary: Block merge (`applyMergeBlocks`) was not updated for the new load-bearing `headingLevel` memory on list-items
samples.evidence: `applyMergeBlocks` (packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:271-276) keeps only the *first* block's attributes, and `MemDocStore.mergeBlock` (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:238) calls it. Reached from `Doc.deleteBackward` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:289). Consequences of the new invariant: (a) Backspace-merging a bulleted heading into the preceding plain bullet silently discards the remembered level, so a later list exit yields a paragraph instead of the heading the diff promises; (b) merging a plain body-text bullet into a bulleted heading makes that body text part of a block that later exits the list as a Heading 2. Neither is covered by the new test file, which only exercises split.

samples.summary: `keepHeadingLevel` writes no `headingLevel` attribute, relying on the tree node already carrying it — a cache/tree divergence would silently lose the level
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1391-1395 derives `keepHeadingLevel` from the cached block and deliberately omits `headingLevel` from the `attrs` written via `tree.styleByPath` (line 1423), while the cache is repopulated at line 1458. Every producer I checked writes the attribute (`blockToAttrs` line 313, `attrsToBlock` line 437, `buildBlockNode` for updateBlock/insert), so I could not construct a concrete divergence; but unlike the `heading` branch (line 1385) this path has no self-healing write, so any future path that sets `block.headingLevel` in the cache only would drop it on the next list toggle. Confirming would need a case where the cached block carries a level the tree node lacks.
